proves: z_index gives a place in the stack only where CSS does
checkable: two 80x40 boxes in a block container. The first is red at x 0..80, y 0..40 and carries z_index 5; the second is blue at x 20..100, y 20..60, pulled up over it by a -20 top margin, and carries 0. Neither is positioned and the parent is block, so CSS 2.1 §9.9.1 gives the 5 nothing to name and document order decides: the overlap at x 20..80, y 20..40 is blue. Under the renderer's previous rule -- every sibling ordered by z_index -- red would paint last and that band would be red instead, which is what makes this image a discriminator rather than a picture of two rectangles.
status: pinnable to arithmetic; stacks_by_z_index() is asserted directly in paint.rs
